## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet. Earlier searches found that 6 of 7 worlds scored exactly 0 for every trial. The only success came from a net that read the mask under several assumed action layouts and summed matching output maps. That suggests the usual deviation is in how action indices map to the grid, not in the recipe. Nothing in this world is ruled out yet. Most other deviations need no special hedge. Permuted obs channels are already absorbed by the learned 1x1 stem, and a different height limit or dynamics shows up in the legality mask, which every candidate reads. So this round tests five layout bets: (1) the reference net unchanged; (2) a 16-layout hedge covering 8 grid symmetries times type-major or type-minor order; (3) a 5x5 head conv for footprint and anchor shifts; (4) the 16-layout hedge plus a learned dense action bias from global features, in case DONE or other actions sit at unexpected indices; (5) the 16-layout hedge plus symmetric views of the obs, in case the obs is transposed or flipped relative to the mask. The sixth candidate (6) combines all of these. All use the reference recipe.

### Round 2
Every round-1 trial scored 0, in dev and in training. Working back from the parameter counts: r1c1 has 53,130 parameters, which gives cin=45, so in_channels=27, Z=6 and T=4. The extra layer in r1c4 adds 16,705 = 65*257, so n_actions=257. So n_place=256=T*Y*X, DONE comes last, and the grid is square. That rules out a different action count or grid size, which means the dense fallback head never ran. Round 1 also covered, and got 0 from: all 8 grid symmetries between obs and action index (the 16-layout re-laying covers them), type-major and type-minor order, a moved DONE via the global bias, and anchor shifts of ±2. Untested: type-middle action orders, dynamics that need footprint-max or longer-range reasoning, a badly scaled obs, and learning speed. This round tests these, one at a time and combined.

### Round 3
All 12 trials scored 0 on dev and in training. The parameter counts fit the spec as described: r1c1's 53,130 parameters need in_channels=27 (Z=6) and n_types=4, and the attention parameters in r2c5 need Y*X=64 with exactly one DONE. So the grid size, action count and DONE count look normal, and the deviation is in what things mean. Ruled out as the only problem: the 24 axis-order and flip action layouts, obs flips and transposes, footprints and anchors within ±2 cells, a moved DONE or global per-action effects, long-range context, and footprint pooling. Channel permutations cannot be the cause, because the 1x1 stem learns any channel order. Still untested: badly scaled obs values, value-loss or reward-scale problems that drown the policy gradient under the global clip, an action order that is not geometric, and vertical dynamics. This round makes one change per bet on top of the 16-layout hedge, plus one combined candidate.

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored exactly 0, in training and on dev, so the deviation is still unfound. The results rule out several causes:
- The action index is not one of the 24 axis orders × 4 flips, read the type-major way or the type-minor way.
- The 3x3 and 5x5 heads did not help, so anchors shifted by up to 2 cells are not the cause.
- Mirrored or transposed obs views did not help.
- A global action bias and flat-mask global logits did not help.
- Reward and obs scale hedges did not help.
- Context blocks, attention, dilated trunks and a per-layer 2.5D branch also stayed at 0.
- 1 PPO epoch did not help.

Three ideas are still untested:
1. A non-dihedral spatial mismatch between the obs and the action grid. I test it with full-scale learned YX→YX token mixing on the obs and in the trunk, plus a dense placement head.
2. Placements offset by one index because DONE comes first, which would also shift the mask. I test a shifted layout set with its own DONE logit at index 0.
3. These hedges combined with a longer-horizon, more-exploratory, more-sample recipe.

This is the last round, so I spread the bets rather than refining.
